title: Medicare Enrollment & Interaction with Employer Plan
source: Dugan K et al. JAMA Network Open. 2025;8(4):e252834 — eAppendix 4
question_text: Do I have to sign up for Medicare when I turn 65, or can I remain on my employer plan?

accurate_complete: Counselor's answer substantively makes clear that the shopper is NOT required to enroll in Medicare and can keep their employer plan
Also discusses Part B implications (e.g., mentions possible late enrollment penalty if employer coverage ends later)
accurate_incomplete: Counselor says the shopper can remain on employer plan and is not required to enroll in Medicare, but does not discuss Part B / late enrollment penalty implications
Says that shopper is not required to enroll in Medicare without elaborating
not_substantive: Counselor said they do not know or otherwise did not substantively answer the question
incorrect: Counselor said that the shopper would be automatically enrolled in Medicare
Said the shopper is required to enroll in Medicare at 65

scoring_notes: The key required fact for Accurate and Complete is both (1) enrollment is optional while on employer coverage, AND (2) mention of Part B / late penalty implications. Omitting the Part B discussion is the most common reason for Accurate but Incomplete. The Incorrect examples listed are material errors that would directly harm a beneficiary's decision.
